+  let awaitingLoad = false
+  let chunksAnnounced = false
+  function sendPlayerLoadedWhenReady () {
+    if (!bot.supportFeature('sendsPlayerLoadedPacket')) return
+    awaitingLoad = true

+  }
+  function checkLoaded () {
+    if (!awaitingLoad || !chunksAnnounced) return
+    const pos = bot.entity?.position
+    if (!pos || !Number.isFinite(pos.x)) return
+    const outsideBuildHeight = pos.y < bot.game.minY || pos.y >= bot.game.minY + bot.game.height

+    awaitingLoad = false
+    chunksAnnounced = false
+    bot._client.write('player_loaded', {})

inline_comments.body:
**Astra agent review — AI-generated, not manually written by the maintainer.**

Please apply the interaction attributes' bounds after evaluating their modifiers. Vanilla sends the base value and modifiers separately, then clamps the effective entity/block interaction range to `[0, 64]` before its reach getters use it ([1.21.4 attribute bounds](https://docs.neoforged.net/docs/1.21.4/entities/attributes/); the same clamp is present in the 1.21.1 attribute implementation).

Through the real `entity_update_attributes` codec and this plugin on 1.21.1 and 1.21.4, entity base `3` plus an additive `-4` modifier makes `entityInteractionRange()` return `-1`. `canInteractWithEntity()` then returns true for a target 0.5 blocks from the eye to its box, because the negative range is squared; vanilla's effective range is zero and the check is false. Block base `4.5` plus `-5.5` has the same problem, while large positive modifiers can exceed the upper bound. Clamp the two interaction getters to their registered bounds and cover an underflow/overflow packet case. The existing generic modifier arithmetic can remain separate.
